newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng '96 operating profit up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng '96 operating profit up 15 pct.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank Ltd said on Monday its operating profit rose by 15.1 percent in 1996 to HK$9.09 billion due to a significant improvement in net interest income and a rise in fees and commissions.
The bank, which is 61.51 percent owned by HSBC Holdings Plc, posted net profit of HK$8.49 billion in 1996, up 6.3 percent.

"Competition in the banking sector further intensified and was especially fierce in the mortgage market, putting interest margins under pressure," Hang Seng Bank's chairman Quo-Wei Lee said in a statement.
"Despite the competitive environment, Hang Seng registered a healthy 15.1 percent growth in operating profit for the year."
Hang Seng said net interest income rose to HK$10.23 billion in 1996 against HK$8.42 billion "mainly due to an encouraging growth in advances to customers and low cost deposits".
It said its net interest margin rose by 30 basis points to 3.10 percent per annum compared with 2.80 percent in 1995.

Other operating income rose by 13.5 percent to HK$2.96 billion mainly due to an increase in fees and commissions receivable, particularly from card, securities and account services and credit facilities.
